title: Chief prosecutor warns giving false addresses in complaints is perjury

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines — Veteran journalist Philip Lustre was deprived of due process when he was indicted and arrested without receiving a copy of the complaint or a chance to defend himself because the complainant provided the wrong address, the chief government prosecutor said Monday. “I would have to agree with them that they were not given due process, as they were not given the opportunity to actually answer the charges against them,” Prosecutor General Richard Anthony Fadullon told reporters. The case involves a cyberlibel complaint in which Lustre was identified as affiliated with the Philippine Daily Inquirer. Because the subpoenas were […]...
